title: New Releases: 5 New Packs from GGG

posts.author: RPGMakerWeb
posts.body:
Five new packs to enhance your games!
​
Do you have a bunch of awesome equipment that you wish showed up on your heroes? Have you ever wanted to use SV movements during a cutscene to add to the moment? Do you love letting your players control the hair colors for their characters? Then you need to check out the Character Generator Expansion Plugin! Min Chieh’Sun is here with a plugin for MZ that puts the power over character outfits into your game, with plugin commands to change things on the fly and options for each piece of equipment to change your party members’ looks without needing to call a common event each time!
There’s so much to be found in this plugin that the included manual is a must-read, but once you get the plugin settings just how you want them you’ll wonder how you ever made games without it! Have your heroes visibly wear the armor they have equipped so your players can easily tell if they remembered to equip their newest set, and have those changes show up in battle, in faceset pictures, and in the menus. And if that wasn’t enough, have some fun with variables to change the color of characters’ eyes and hair and add balloons and other emotion-announcing icons to their message box pictures so that it’s easy to tell just what a party member is feeling. If you’ve been searching for a plugin to give you more control over character appearances or you just are tired of making tons of versions of your heroes for each possible outfit combination, check out the Character Generator Expansion Plugin!

​
Give your inventory a new look with Listhobi's Adventuring Supplies! Liam Steven Holt Bibby joins the scene with an iconset that reimagines MV’s default icons into colorful pixel art. Replace your plain state icons with pops of color, with bright green poison bubbles and a deep purple skull for fear, and give your buffs and debuffs an actual design instead of simple up and down arrows. Most of MV’s icons have a matching replacement in this iconset so you can easily replace the default and not need to worry about adjusting every database item! Besides the remakes, this pack also includes a bunch of unique weapon icons so your heroes can have a variety of equipment choices. Let your hero choose from bronze, steel, and poisoned blades, or keep things simple with a selection of elemental greatswords to switch between depending on the enemy.
Still want more icons for all your monster drops and resource harvesting points? Then make use of this iconset’s recolors, where most of the resources come in all the colors of the rainbow along with white, gray, and black options! Let your players find all sorts of gems in underground dungeons and gather a number of powders to help craft new and stronger potions. Or offer more than 100 rings with different gemstones and metal band colors that can affect party members’ skills, buffs, and resistances! This pack also includes a window skin with golden edges and crystals in the corner so your treasure-hunting adventurers can have a suitably shiny message box and menu. Check out Listhobi's Adventuring Supplies if you want a different look for your items or want a ton of color options for accessories and monster drops!

​
Step back in time to the world of Edo with the Minikle Backgrounds Bundle EDO part02 A pack! Minikle is back with another pack of pictures, this time giving us 34 exterior images to help set the scene in a world inspired by historical Japan. 8 different locations come with multiple versions based on time and weather, so you can let your players know that time has passed without having to tell them with words. Enjoy a sunset from the comfort of a tiled roof while hiding from boring chores, visit a loved one’s grave as blue skies turn to a cloudy gray and eventually run for cover through dirt streets lit by red lanterns as rain pours down from above.
Have your heroine meet with a close friend in front of their red houses and walk by the house’s exterior hallways that are protected by a lattice of wood, or have them climb up onto the black tiled roof to chat away from the prying eyes of strangers. Stop by the rows of townhouses to catch up on the latest gossip, and walk through a graveyard of tall stone monuments to say goodbye to a father figure. Each image comes in 2 sizes, 816x614 and 1280x720, so you can add them to your favorite RPG Maker engine even if you’re not using the default screen size. Pick up Minikle Backgrounds Bundle EDO part02 A to add even more cutscene backgrounds to your game!

​
After a long day of fighting monsters in a fantasy land or dealing with politics in a historical drama, let your heroes rest in comfortable interiors with the Minikle Backgrounds Bundle EDO part02 B pack! Minikle has even more pictures inspired by historical Japan to share with us, focusing on interior shots this time! 38 images offer up a selection of angles from 2 rooms to help tell your story. Have your hero explore the room they’re staying in closely, possibly finding an important clue or useful item tucked away somewhere safe, and let them train in a huge room to learn a new sword technique from a master!
Each image has multiple versions so you can show the time of day, so you can set up a scene where your hero is woken up in the middle of the night long after the lights have been put out or show that a party member trained from dawn until dusk to learn a new skill. Use the different angles to let your players know when two characters step away to speak privately and depending on your battle system you could even use some of these as battle backgrounds! 2 sizes, 816x614 and 1280x720, for each image makes it simple to choose the best option for your RPG Maker game. If you’ve been needing a good room for training sequences or want to have a relaxing cutscene with shoji screens blocking the outside world and tatami mats making for a comfortable floor, pick up Minikle Backgrounds Bundle EDO part02 B!

​
Visit towns of mushrooms, fairy gardens, and spooky abandoned towns with the NEONPIXEL - Mixed Tile Assets pack! Neonpixel is back with a collection of B sheets that can add more fun details and interesting buildings to your maps. Build a secret forest town filled with towering mushrooms in the trees, a decrepit stone hospital surrounded by dead stumps, a forest clearing filled with roses and statues, and more with this pack!
7 B sheets are filled with nature tiles and some buildings to help turn an empty map into a location that is really important to the game’s story. Explore acres of forest where evergreen trees slowly decrease and deciduous trees with lush and puffy branches of leaves take their place, or create a trail of trees with unusual square leaf bunches that your players can follow to find a hidden cave! Build a vibrant village full of colorful roses, and wooden and mushroom houses, or create destroyed towns where trees have grown through the houses’ roofs and the graveyard is full of headstones and snarling gargoyles.
Also included in this pack are 17 character sprite animations for plants and fog to add more movement to your maps. Have blue roses flutter in place to show an invisible breeze through a town, or have trees shake to show when a monster is hiding in them to warn your players about a potential fight. So if you need some flower patches and more trees to fill your forests, or just want to complete your NEONPIXEL set, check out the NEONPIXEL - Mixed Tile Assets pack!

posts.author: KoriCongo
posts.body: How does the CG Expansion pack compare to other character creator plugins around? Can you adjust individual layers midgame?

posts.author: sunhihi
posts.body:
ATT_Turan said:
That character generator expansion plugin looks really neat.
Are there any limitations/requirements that it would have to work with image dimensions equivalent to the included character generator in MZ? Or can it work with other sizes so long as the file names and layering system is adhered to?
Click to expand...
The file name should preferably not contain any special characters, as well as be purely numeric.
For example: 00#$R or 000000 or 17.88
KoriCongo said:
How does the CG Expansion pack compare to other character creator plugins around? Can you adjust individual layers midgame?
Click to expand...
Compared to other character plugins, its layer structure is completely freeform. However, setting up equipment binding or variables is extremely intricate and requires complex plugin configurations.
Since it operates entirely based on plugin settings, it naturally cannot allow you to sculpt faces in the game. However, it does have a feature that is even better than sculpting faces in-game—its scope includes TVD, and it also considers the function of invoking SV graphics.
